prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Sentinel Vale: ground-only land/coastal/cryosphere imagery; predictable latency,documented quality,external interfaces retained. Elements: Mission Control Center(Bluebell/local voice)—safety/pass/anomaly supervision,command release,schedules,primary routing; Flight Dynamics Facility(Mistral/legacy logs)—navigation/maneuvers,sends visibility predictions/antenna pointing products before execution release; Mission Planning System—demand/constraints→plans,receives contact booking requests(service,antenna,elevation,volume,priority); Command Validation Gateway—mandatory pre-uplink checks; Network Control System(Lantern)—authoritative circuit status,routing,allocations/readiness/contact records,path/maintenance visibility; Ground Network Manager(Juniper/rosters)—availability/conflicts/maintenance/staffing,issues Antenna Deicing Notice,pins maintenance-critical pre-acquisition tasks; Orbit Determination Engine—tracking→orbit knowledge,qualified passes→Doppler Residual Report; Telemetry Ingest Service—receives spacecraft telemetry/contact status/data-flow indicators,supplies operations/engineering/processing,distinguishes gaps/interruptions; Payload Processing Facility—processing/calibration/distribution,coordinates Primary Processing Cluster(nominal)/Backup Processing Cluster(controlled failover); Product Quality Service—pre-distribution checks; Long Term Archive—authoritative data/products/evidence; User Services Portal—search/orders/status/support. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team—safety/authorization; Flight Dynamics Team—navigation,timing/orbit monitoring separating clock bias from tracking error; Payload Calibration Team—quality; Cybersecurity Desk—monitoring/escalation,sends Security Exception Ticket for temporary baseline deviations; local station teams—configuration/frequencies/time/interlocks/logs; station operators→Mission Control Center constraints. Antennas: North S-Band Antenna(nominal command/telemetry),South S-Band Antenna(procedure-compatible alternate)→Mission Control Center through protected mission/administration-separated routers; Kiruna X-Band Antenna(European payload),Svalbard X-Band Antenna(longer northern visibility/lower losses)→Payload Processing Facility over dual carrier-outage-surviving paths. Redundant terrestrial interconnections; performance reviews require corrections. Requirements: continuous safety/pass coverage; business-hours/on-call engineering; autonomous routines,human command/major-change authorization; controlled configurations/procedures,duty segregation,evidence,rehearsals,redundancy verification; daily freeze,approved justified contingencies; safety→timeliness→efficiency. Contacts

Document units:
S078: The North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna are normally assigned for command and low-rate telemetry contacts, while the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna support high-rate telemetry reception when the visibility geometry and data volume justify their use.
S079: The Network Control System provides the Mission Control Center with antenna status, link configuration, timing references, and routing readiness before each pass begins.
S080: The Telemetry Ingest Service accepts real-time frames, validates basic framing and time continuity, and records reception metadata needed for later operational review.
S081: The Telemetry Ingest Service produces the Pass Replay Packet after a contact when the received stream must be reconstructed for engineering review.
S082: During live operations, the Spacecraft Operations Team monitors spacecraft mode, power state, thermal margins, attitude indicators, command counters, onboard storage, and fault protection messages from the Mission Control Center consoles.
S083: Console displays emphasize deviations from expected state rather than raw parameter volume, because operators must identify safety trends while a contact is still available.
S084: The console lead is responsible for declaring pass status, authorizing planned command execution through the Command Validation Gateway, and pausing the activity when telemetry does not match the expected configuration.
S085: The telemetry engineer verifies reception quality, frame loss, latency, and stream continuity, and advises the console lead when degraded link conditions could affect command confidence.
S086: The spacecraft systems engineer interprets health telemetry, confirms that subsystem states remain within flight rules, and records any anomaly context needed by subsystem specialists.
S087: The Ground Network Manager remains accountable for antenna assignment, ground link availability, and coordination with site operations when weather, equipment status, or routing issues affect a contact.
S088: The Flight Dynamics Team uses tracking measurements and validated time tags from the contact to support orbit assessment at the Flight Dynamics Facility.
S089: The Orbit Determination Engine supports routine state updates and provides the basis for predicting future visibility periods, maneuver planning constraints, and antenna pointing expectations.
S090: Pass reconstruction begins when the contact closes and combines command history, received telemetry timing, ground station status, and operator log entries into a single operational narrative.
S091: The reconstructed pass record is used to confirm whether planned objectives were completed, whether any onboard event occurred outside the timeline, and whether additional engineering analysis is required.
S092: The Payload Processing Facility is also known operationally as Forgehouse in console discussions and shift logs.
